and Being Surprised by Certain Easter Eggs|author=Davids, Brian|date=2022-11-09|work=[[Wikipedia:The Hollywood Reporter|''The Hollywood Reporter'']]|archivedate=20221109220924}}</ref> He wanted Mothma and the other legacy characters to not provide fan service.<ref name="Real People">{{WebCite|url=https://variety.com/2022/tv/news/star-wars-andor-tony-gilroy-diego-luna-1235348148|text=How ‘Andor' Became the First ‘Star Wars' TV Series for Grown-Ups: ‘I Wanted to Do It About Real People'|author=Vary, Adam B|work=[[Wikipedia:Variety (magazine)|''Variety'']]|archivedate=20220824140042}}</ref> Executive producer [[Sanne Wohlenberg]] and her team put much thought into how they would represent Mothma and show her journey, and they stayed aware of where she ended up in ''Rogue One''.<ref name="ProductionBrief" />

[[File:MonMothmaCostumeSDCC.jpg|thumb|right|260px|Mon Mothma's costume was designed by Michael Wilkinson.]]
Production designer [[Luke Hull]] created a sketch of Mon Mothma exiting a Senate limousine on Coruscant.<ref name="Period drama">{{WebCite|url=https://www.theverge.com/23445550/star-wars-andor-production-costume-design-interview|text=Andor's designers approached it like a Star Wars period drama|author=Webster, Andrew|work=[[Wikipedia:The Verge|''The Verge'']]|archivedate=20221109181234}}</ref> Costume designer [[Michael Wilkinson]] styled Mothma in flowing robes that evoked her sense of style seen in her ''Revenge of the Sith'' deleted scene. He knew that Mothma was a senator from Chandrila who was stationed on Coruscant, so he thought about people from different countries that work at the [[Wikipedia:Headquarters of the United Nations|United Nations building]] in [[Wikipedia:New York|New York]]. Wilkinson's team intended to bring elements of clothing from Mothma's home, so they came up with a set of colors and textures mainly drawn from other iterations of her. He leaned into pale neutral tones, and Mothma was given slightly shimmery organic textures with hints of metals.<ref name="Dressing the galaxy">{{SW|url=news/dressing-the-galaxy-designer-michael-wilkinson-defines-the-look-of-andor-s-costumes|text=Dressing the Galaxy: Designer Michael Wilkinson Defines the Look of <i>Andor</i>'s Costumes}}</ref>

The crew tried to show Mothma's public face and the private woman within it.<ref name="Never thought">{{WebCite|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-features/andor-star-genevieve-oreilly-never-thought-shed-get-the-chance-to-flesh-out-mon-mothma-1235221270|text=‘Andor' Star Genevieve O'Reilly Never Thought She'd Get the Chance to Flesh Out Mon Mothma|author=Davids, Brian|date=2022-09-15|work=[[Wikipedia:The Hollywood Reporter|''The Hollywood Reporter'']]|archivedate=20220915165314}}</ref> O'Reilly was delighted to have an opportunity to better understand her character.<ref name="ProductionBrief" /> She also wanted to explore Mothma as a Rebel leader and as a woman,<ref name="Never thought" /> which included showing the private face of someone who navigates through systems of oppression.<ref name="Potent Moment">{{SW|url=news/andor-launch-interview-gilroy-and-cast|text="A Potent Moment in History": Insights from Tony Gilroy and the ''Andor'' Cast}}</ref> O'Reilly tried to understand the pain and personal cost felt by Caroline Blakiston in ''Return of the Jedi'', and she enjoyed learning more about Mothma's life.<ref name="Never thought" /> She was excited for the audience to see Mothma's journey of becoming the Rebel leader that she is in ''Rogue One''.<ref name="Potent Moment" /> O'Reilly wanted her character's new look in the show to reflect her new stage as a successful member of high society.<ref name="Marriage" /> Scenes in the Chandrilan embassy were filmed in a practically built set that had a wraparound [[Wikipedia:Light-emitting diode|LED]] screen that used [[Wikipedia:StageCraft|StageCraft]] technology.<ref name="Slashfilm">{{WebCite|url=https://www.slashfilm.com/1090902/heres-where-andor-actually-used-lucasfilms-stagecraft-technology-exclusive|text=Here's Where Andor Actually Used Lucasfilm's StageCraft Technology [Exclusive]|author=Meyer, Joshua|date=2022-11-09|work=[[Wikipedia:/Film|''/Film'']]|archivedate=20221109201335}}</ref>

Composer [[Nicholas Britell]] created a musical signature for Mothma.<ref name="Rustling leaves">{{WebCite|url=https://variety.com/2022/artisans/news/andor-composer-nicholas-britell-score-star-wars-1235383443|text=‘Andor' Composer Nicholas Britell Breaks Down His Score and Why He Incorporated Rustling Leaves|author=Burlingame, Jon|date=2022-09-26|work=[[Wikipedia:Variety (magazine)|''Variety'']]|archivedate=20220926170019}}</ref> For [[Andor Season 2|Season Two]], Michael Wilkinson worked on costumes that would evolve Mothma into the leader of the Rebellion.<ref name="Dressing the galaxy" /> In an interview with ''Tech Radar'', O'Reilly and [[Faye Marsay]]—who played Mothma's cousin [[Vel Sartha]] in the series—reflected on their characters, with Marsay saying that, to Sartha, their relationship was not difficult and instead was one of tough circumstances: while Sartha acted on the frontlines of rebellion, Mothma was more in the shadows.<ref name="Many cards">{{WebCite|url=https://www.techradar.com/streaming/disney-plus/hes-holding-a-lot-of-the-cards-andor-stars-tease-luthens-important-role-in-the-evolution-of-mon-mothma-and-vel-sarthas-familial-dynamic|text='He's holding a lot of the cards': Andor stars tease Luthen's 'important' role in the evolution of Mon Mothma and Vel Sartha's familial dynamic|author=Power, Tom|date=2025-04-22|work=''Tech Radar''|archivedate=20250501215700}}</ref> Factoring in Mothma's mother in regards to Leida's wedding, O'Reilly mentioned how "within the dialogue" there were "three generations of women," which turned the scene into a very "interconnected, intergenerational story." Further, she had pushed Gilroy to give Mothma a scene in which she gave Leida an out of the wedding, which culminated in the scene where Mothma does, but Leida gives what O'Reilly reflected to be a "pretty brutal" response.<ref name="YahooNews">{{WebCite|url=https://ca.news.yahoo.com/andor-star-genevieve-oreilly-on-leidas-pretty-brutal-response-to-mon-mothma-before-wedding-021432659.html|text='Andor' star Genevieve O'Reilly on Leida's 'pretty brutal' response to Mon Mothma before wedding|author=Elisabetta Bianchini|date=2025-04-25|work=''Yahoo'' News|archivedate=20250424030919}}</ref> After the conclusion of ''Andor'', O'Reilly reflected on the wonderful surprise that returning to ''Star Wars'' had been and how ''Andor'' revealed more about Mothma to her. While she was unsure if it was possible to push Mothma's character further, she was open to the idea of returning once again.<ref name="Goldderby">{{WebCite|url=https://www.goldderby.com/article/2025/andor-star-genevieve-oreilly-on-her-unlikely-two-decade-mon-mothma-journey-ive-closed-the-circle-on-her|text=‘Andor' star Genevieve O'Reilly on her unlikely two-decade Mon Mothma journey: ‘I've closed the circle on her'|author=Scott Huver|date=2025-06-06|work=GoldDerby|archivedate=20250609222729}}</ref>

===Discrepancies===
{{Quote|Bail Organa of Alderaan. How long have you known him?''"<br />"''Since I first joined the Senate, I suppose.''"<br />"''And how long ago was that?''"<br />"''You know the answer.''"<br />"''How long ago, please?''"<br />"''Thirteen years? Just about.|Mon Mothma, under Imperial interrogation|<ref name="MOF" />}}
According to ''[[Star Wars: The Rebel Files]]'', Mothma was elected senator in "[[Imperial calendar|8 BFE]]," i.e. 8 [[Standard year|years]] before the [[Proclamation of the New Order|proclamation]] of the [[Galactic Empire]]<ref name="Rebel Files" /> in [[19 BBY]],<ref name="Galactic Atlas">''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]''</ref> which would place her election in [[27 BBY]].<ref name="Rebel Files" /><ref name="Galactic Atlas" /> However, in the novel ''[[Queen's Shadow]]'', Mon Mothma says that she was "very new to the Senate when [Padmé Amidala] made [her] speech as Queen of Naboo,"<ref name="Queen's Shadow">''[[Queen's Shadow]]''</ref> referring to a scene of the movie [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']].<ref name="Episode I">{{Film|I}}</ref> According to ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]'', the events of the movie took place in [[32 BBY]],<ref name="Galactic Atlas" /> which would place Mothma's election that year or earlier.<ref name="Queen's Shadow" /><ref name="Galactic Atlas" /> In ''[[Reign of the Empire: The Mask of Fear]]'', the novel's events taking place in 19 BBY, Mothma stated that she joined the Senate nearly thirteen years ago, also placing her election circa 32 BBY.<ref name="MOF" />

In the novel ''[[Leia, Princess of Alderaan]]'', both Mothma and Winmey Lenz are identified as the Senior Senator of Chandrila.<ref name="Leia Princess of Alderaan" /> "[[Welcome to the Rebellion]]" went onto corroborate that it was Mothma who served as Senior Senator.<ref name="Welcome to the Rebellion" /> As such, this article assumes Mothma acted as Senior Senator, not Lenz.

===Role in ''Star Wars'' Legends===
{{Quote|This great struggle is a people's struggle: a struggle between the strong and the weak, the rich and the poor, the cruel and the gentle.|Mon Mothma, describing the Rebellion in a quote from the ''[[The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook]]''|<ref name="TRAS">''[[The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Bail_Organa_and_Mon_Mothma.jpg|thumb|150px|Mon Mothma and Bail Organa, in an image from ''The New Essential Chronology'']]
[[Mon Mothma/Legends|Mon Mothma]] appeared in numerous stories in the Expanded Universe of books, comics, and games, which have since become non-canon and rebranded as [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]].<ref name="Legends Announcement">{{SW|url=news/the-legendary-star-wars-expanded-universe-turns-a-new-page|text=The Legendary Star Wars Expanded Universe Turns a New Page}}</ref> These stories saw her role in the Rebellion fleshed out, showing her as the leader of the Rebel Alliance. The [[1991]] novel ''[[Heir to the Empire]]'', written by [[Timothy Zahn]], showed her becoming [[Chancellor (New Republic)|Chief of State]] of the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]],<ref name="Heir to the Empire">''[[Heir to the Empire]]''</ref> setting the stage for her canonical counterpart to become the first chancellor of the New Republic.<ref name="Aftermath" /> The 2005 reference book ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' established that the Legends version of Mon Mothma died in her sleep [[24 ABY/Legends|twenty years]] after the Battle of Endor.<ref name="nec">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> After the character continued appearing in Legends stories, Blakiston became aware of her character's prolific appearances. She was intrigued by this fact<ref name="Blakiston interview" /><ref name="Knightley" /> and credited it to what she saw as Mothma's strong personality. Blakiston stated that, despite the character's limited screentime in ''Return of the Jedi'', she saw Mothma as an archetypal figure not unlike Darth Vader and Obi-Wan Kenobi.<ref name="Knightley" />
